public.text: Operational governance is accountable for infrastructure integrity, safe change and evaluation in use, but the monitoring scope is not explicit at the architecture-to-care interface. Availability, data quality and standards conformance alone may miss unsafe workarounds, delayed or missed care, documentation burden, near misses, inequitable access and deterioration in clinically meaningful outcomes.
public.suggestedRevision: Expand operational monitoring to include point-of-care consequences: downtime and degraded-service effects; workarounds and override patterns; delayed or missed care; near misses and adverse events; clinical workload and usability burden; equity of access; and clinically meaningful outcome drift. Require feedback from frontline clinicians and service users, with findings feeding operational correction and strategic review.
